sentences.text: 1 "i) Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction to the respondent nos.2 and 3 to redetermine the compensation amount in accordance with the direction issued by this Hon'ble Court in its order dated 12.05.2010 and pay the same to the petitioner company.

i a) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari for the quashing of the order of respondent no.2 dated 11.11.2022 (Annexure No.1 of the compliance affidavit annexed as Annexure No.7 to the writ petition)"
3.
Earlier the petitioner had approached this Court by means of Writ (C) No.21084 of 2004, (Ram Charan @ Ram Chandra versus State of U.P. and others).

entities.text: Ram Charan @ Ram Chandra versus State of U.P. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was disposed of by the following order dated 12.05.2010 :-
"Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record.

Perusal of record shows that the possession has been taken over though without complying the provisions of Section 10(3) and 10(5) of the Urban Land (Ceiling &
Regulation) Act, 1976 therefore, the possession was illegal.

However, since the Moradabad Development Authority has taken over the possession and has raised the construction, therefore, Moradabad Development Authority is ready to pay the compensation or land in lieu thereof whichever is convenient and feasible in the circumstances.

Considering the facts and circumstances, but without prejudice to the merits of the case, Moradabad Development Authority is directed to either give compensation at the rate of market value prevalent today or provide the land in lieu thereof within a period of one month from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
With aforesaid observation the writ petition if finally disposed of. "
4. The above order has attained finality upon disposal of Special Leave to Appeal (C) No.1334 of 2011, (Moradabad Development Authority through Vice Chairman versus Ram Charan @ Ram Chander (D) TR. LRS. & ORS) vide order dated 28.03.2016, passed by the Supreme Court.
5.

sentences.text: In such circumstances, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner claims, petitioner is entitled to payment of compensation to be computed at the market rate without treating the situation to be one covered under the land acquisition laws.

Since market rate was required to be paid under judicial order passed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the respondents were duty bound to make that computation without reference to the circle rate.

6. Also it is his submission, as of now, the present petitioner is entitled to the compensation amount as the original owner (respondent nos.4 and 5) had executed a valid sale deed in favour of the petitioner, on 03.06.2016.

sentences.text: 2 7. Pursuant to the last order, Sri Dharmendra Singh Chauhan, learned counsel for the respondent nos.2 & 3 (Development Authority) and Sri I.N. Singh, learned counsel for the respondent nos.4 and 5 have obtained instructions from the contesting respondents.

At the outset, Sri I.N. Singh, learned counsel for the respondent nos.4 and 5 has filed a personal affidavit of private respondent no.4 on his own behalf and also on behalf of private respondent no.5.

In paragraph nos.2 and 3 of the said affidavit, it has been stated as below :-
2.

That the erstwhile owner of the land in question was Ram Charan @ Ram Chander when this Hon'ble Court had passed the order dated 12.05.2010 and after his death his two sons, Harpal Singh (respondent no.4) and Balbir Singh (since deceased)
became his legal heirs.

After the death of Balbir Singh his wife respondent no.5 became his legal heir and representative and her such status has also been recognized by the respondent nos.2 and 3, as is evident from the impugned order /
communication dated 11.11.2022.
3. That since the deponent and his deceased brother Balbir Singh had already sold the land in question to the petitioner Company by executing a sale deed dated 03.06.2016 in its favour, the deponent and respondent no.5 have no objection if the compensation of the said land is paid to the petitioner Company."
8. In turn Sri Dharmendra Singh Chauhan, learned counsel for the respondent - Development Authority states an error has occurred in computation of the compensation amount.
The same had be computed at the market value.

He therefore prays for opportunity to be granted to the Development Authority to rectify the mistake and make a fresh computation in accordance with the order passed by the writ Court in Writ (C) No.21084 of 2004, (Ram Charan @ Ram Chandra versus State of U.P. and others) noted above.
9.

entities.text: Ram Charan @ Ram Chandra versus State of U.P. and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above statements made by learned Standing Counsel, no dispute survives for adjudication by this Court.
10. Accordingly, the order dated 11.11.2022 is set aside.
The matter is remitted to the Development Authority to pass a fresh order with respect to the amount of compensation to be computed and paid to the petitioner.

Also in view of the statement made by learned counsel for the private respondent nos.4 and 5, that compensation amount may be paid out to the petitioner who may simultaneously execute the sale deed in favour of the petitioner, since facts are not in dispute, let such exercise be completed within a period of three month from today.
11. With the aforesaid observations and directions, the writ petition is disposed of.
